mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the past 3 months indicates active monetary easing, reducing discount rates and boosting equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods with 3-month FEDFUNDS decline, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When unemployment rate exceeds 4.5% in a single month, it signals deteriorating labor conditions that trigger corporate cost-cutting and earnings declines, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of months with UNRATE > 4.5%, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous decline in residential construction permits (HOUST) and rise in consumer credit (RSAFS) indicates housing market weakness and credit tightening, predicting negative S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances with HOUST decline >2% and RSAFS rise >1%, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: During industrial contraction (INDPRO < 100), S&P 500 underperforms over 20 trading days due to reduced corporate output and earnings growth, but this effect is absent in expansionary supply regimes.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods with INDPRO < 100, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When consumer credit (RSAFS) increases by more than 2% month-over-month, it signals rising consumer spending and economic optimism, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of months with RSAFS rise > 2%, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Sustained growth in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) over 3 months indicates strengthening labor markets that support consumer spending and corporate earnings, producing positive S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods with 3-month PAYEMS growth, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In high-inflation (CPIAUCSL YoY > 3.5%) and aggressive tightening (FEDFUNDS > 4.0%) regimes, S&P 500 experiences negative returns over 60 trading days due to rising real rates and profit margin pressure.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods with CPIAUCSL YoY > 3.5% and FEDFUNDS > 4.0%, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent industrial production decline (INDPRO < 100) and unemployment rise (UNRATE > 4.0%) signal dual supply-labor market contraction, predicting negative S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances with INDPRO < 100 and UNRATE > 4.0%, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
